title: Unit Mismatch: $$SM_{FORCES}$$ Output
body: On September $$23$$, $$1999$$, while attempting to guide a probe into its planned orbit around Mars, NASA lost contact with it. Subsequent investigations showed a piece of software called $$SM_{FORCES}$$ (or “small forces”) was recording thruster performance data in the English units of pound-force·seconds ($$\text{lbf}\cdot\text{s}$$). However, other pieces of software that used these values for course corrections expected them to be recorded in the SI units of newton·seconds ($$\text{N}\cdot\text{s}$$), as dictated in the software interface protocols. (A 'pound-force' (lbf) is a unit of force equal to the gravitational force on one pound of mass on earth.) $$1\, \text{lbf}$$ is approximately $$4.45\, \text{N}$$.
